rulings: Diagnosis 2026-09-19 (staging smoke case 4, run 35472361102 vs prior-pass 35469045247): the query "2026 Bowman Chrome Owen Carey Black BCP-69" priced at $12.50 where the smoke pins it withheld. Root cause traced to the pool at hobbyiqCardId hiq:baseball:2026:bowman:bcp-69:black-refractor:no-auto (42 sold_comps rows), NOT to PR #2330 (which only adds an exclusion filter) and not a stale smoke pin.

CF-THE-TITLE-OUTRANKS-THE-VENDOR-TAG (repair-parallel-from-title.cjs doctrine, Drew 2026-08-29): 41 of the 42 rows are CardHedge sales whose title never says 'Black' -- every one reads 'Mojo Refractor' (35 rows, both cardhedge sourceExternalId groups 1780156975067x514711415448764200 and one row's group) or 'Laser Refractor' / 'Lazer Refractor' (6 rows, cardhedge group 1778477514892x343483198805100600). Re-parsing every title with the repo's own ebayTitleParser.service.js's parseListingTitle confirms this split exactly (35 'Mojo Refractor', 6 'Lazer Refractor', 1 'Black X-Fractor' -- see per-row evidence).

repair-parallel-from-title.cjs's own COLOURS list (Gold/Blue/Black/Silver/etc. bare-and-refractor forms) does not include named finishes ('Mojo', 'Lazer/Laser', 'Reptilian', etc.), so this specific mislabel class was out of that script's measured scope and was never caught by its colours-mode runs. This list is the targeted, report-reviewed fix for this one card's pool, built the same way that script would (title-parse wins over the stored vendor/product tag) but scoped by hand to entries a human reviewed.

ONE AXIS PER ENTRY, product segment untouched (R75/'a relocation list changes only the ruled axis'): every entry below keeps the hiq id's PRODUCT segment (index 3, 'bowman') exactly as the row's current hobbyiqCardId already has it. Nothing here relocates a row's cardId partition or changes which product it is filed under -- only the parallel (and, for the one numbered row, its num- tail, which is inherent to that parallel identity, not a separate axis) is corrected to what the row's own title states.

Lazer Refractor (6 rows, REPOINT): destination hiq:baseball:2026:bowman:bcp-69:lazer-refractor:no-auto exists as a checklist-backed card_catalog row (source=hobbymonitor-scraped-2026-08-31, playerName=Owen Carey, setKey=bowman). Every one of the 6 rows is already partitioned under a raw CardHedge vendor id (cardId=1778477514892x343483198805100600, not an hiq slug), so only hobbyiqCardId needs correcting -- REPOINT, not RELOCATE.

Black X-Fractor /10 (1 row, REPOINT): the one genuine card in this pool -- cardsight title '2026 1st Bowman Owen Carey Chrome X-Fractor BLACK # /10 #BCP-69 Braves', $199.99 -- carries reslugedFrom=hiq:baseball:2026:bowman-chrome:bcp-69:black-refractor:no-auto:num-10 (reslugedAt 2026-08-29), then a later, unrelated bowman-chrome->bowman product repointing (CF-IT-CAME-OUT-OF-BOWMAN, repair-bowman-product-refile.cjs, reslugedAt 2026-09-06) carried it and the 41 contaminated Mojo/Lazer rows onto today's shared hiq:baseball:2026:bowman:bcp-69:black-refractor:no-auto address, silently dropping the /10 print-run identity. Destination hiq:baseball:2026:bowman:bcp-69:black-x-fractor:no-auto:num-10 exists as a checklist-backed card_catalog row (source=hobbymonitor-scraped-2026-08-31, playerName=Owen Carey, setKey=bowman, printRun=10) with the product segment (bowman) already matching this row's current address -- so this is a parallel+num-tail identity correction, not a product move. This row's cardId partition key is itself an hiq slug (hiq:baseball:2026:bowman-chrome:bcp-69:base:no-auto:num-10, unrelated to today's diagnosis and NOT touched here) so this too is a hobbyiqCardId-only REPOINT.

Mojo Refractor (35 rows, HELD OUT): no checklist-backed card_catalog row exists at hiq:baseball:2026:bowman:bcp-69:mojo-refractor:no-auto (bare 'Mojo Refractor' under the plain bowman product). The bowman-stock checklist's Mojo Refractor insert for BCP-69 is catalogued under a compound insert-set name (hiq:baseball:2026:bowman:bcp-69:mega-chrome-prospects-mojo:no-auto, source=checklistcenter, playerName=Owen Carey) -- a DIFFERENT parallel slug than the title parser produces, and reconciling that naming gap is a catalog-vocabulary question, not a one-axis pool relocation. A bare-'Mojo Refractor' catalog row exists only under bowman-chrome / bowman-chrome-mega-box product segments (hiq:baseball:2026:bowman-chrome:bcp-69:mojo-refractor:no-auto and the -mega-box sibling), which would require ALSO changing the product segment -- explicitly out of scope for a one-axis list (see the companion R75 program, which handles product-segment moves separately). Held out per instructions rather than guessed.

Follow-up (read-only, paged, no aggregates, 10-minute budget, both pages completed within budget): 2026 sold_comps rows carrying a ':mojo' fragment in hobbyiqCardId under the bowman product family -- hiq:baseball:2026:bowman: 9,326 rows, hiq:baseball:2026:bowman-chrome: 3,918 rows, TOTAL 13,244. This is the scale of the product-segment/insert-naming reconciliation a future product-axis list would need to cover; the 35 held-out rows here are a small fraction of it and were not counted separately within this figure.
